handoff.uncertainty_reduced: Whether the executed run package can be archived at all: a ledger that does not validate blocks the snapshot, the blinded review round, and the disposition. This task removes that block and nothing else.
handoff.why_this_task_exists: The frozen contract's required_artifacts clause names "runs/*/manifest.yaml, code.command + code.commit + dirty-tree state" but never names the ledger's nested `run:` schema, so the drivers satisfied the contract and still failed tools/validate_ledger.py. The defect is SCHEMA CONFORMANCE ONLY. It is not evidence about H-ECRANK-ee6e0e, not a control failure, not an invalidation under IV-1..IV-7, and not a re-scoring of any run (core rules 3 and 5). Because the manifests are still UNCOMMITTED worker output, they are repaired in place before any archive binds them; no durable record is edited and no supersession entry is created. The contract-wording gap is recorded for the closing decision DEC-20260906-7448cf so the next frozen contract names the schema.
inputs: tools/validate_ledger.py (check_run and RUN_REQUIRED_TOP: the target schema)
experiments/EXP-ALBIN-001/runs/RUN-ALBIN-001-import/manifest.yaml (a committed schema-compliant exemplar of the nested run record and its companion files)
constraints: NO RE-SCORING, EVER. Every number, timestamp, seed, sha256, counter, validity string, and resource measurement already recorded stays byte-equivalent in meaning: the repair MOVES fields into the nested shape, it never edits, rounds, recomputes, backfills, or drops one. Where the schema needs a field the flat manifest does not carry, the value is derived ONLY from an existing recorded field of the same run (for example command.txt from code.command, environment.json from the environment block) and the derivation is named in the mapping note.

Core rule 9: fabricate nothing. A field whose value does not already exist in that run's recorded artifacts is written as an explicit null with a sibling note saying the run did not record it -- never guessed.

Never record a kind the run does not assert.

Do NOT touch raw-result.json, stdout.log, stderr.log, checkpoints/, diagnostics/, determinism-diff.txt, the attempt-*/ failure directories or their manifests, certificates/, source/, execution-report.yaml, the frozen specification.yaml, or anything outside the experiment directory. review_plan.claim_under_review: The executor's run records for EXP-ECRANK-76a70d v1: whether the decidable success criterion was met or missed EXACTLY as frozen (arm B: >= 1 nonsingular quartic with 8 forced non-torsion points across 4 distinct twist classes of one k=3 coset inside the frozen box/caps, exact descent-free certificate reporting certified k=3 total >= 8 from the forced classes with the eigenspace/F_l split, zero verifier errors, all controls IV-1..IV-7 untriggered), and nothing beyond it. This round reviews the RUN RECORDS only: it does NOT promote C1, does NOT close anything, and does NOT touch the UNPROMOTED closure candidate of DEC-20260905-7adca0 -- any breakthrough/closure-tier promotion remains separately gated behind IMP-2 (review-breakthrough at max, never degraded).
review_plan.coordinator_prior: Recorded BEFORE any reviewer runs. Expected: the instrument smoke self-test passes on committed fixtures; IV-1 known-false d=(1..1) reports total = n exactly (7 at n=8, 9 at n=10) -- I expect this to PASS because the certificate machinery is the committed verifier stack reused from EXP-ECRANK-e1e30e; the determinism re-run matches bit-for-bit; arms A and B complete inside the counted-op cap at the assumed >= 2 x 10^4 ops/s floor (finding 2's disclosed assumption -- if the real engine is slower I expect inert exhaustion with an honestly reported completed prefix, NOT a fake result). Arm B success itself is GENUINELY UNCERTAIN: the design derived P(zero | rate >= q) ~ 4.5e-5 for the positive branch at the declared floor q = 10^-3, but the true density may sit below q, in which case I expect an honest negative or exhausted-prefix report. Arm C (n=10, exponent 0) is borderline by design: a null there is a P3-relevant measurement, not an invalidation. Where I think a failure would hide, if there is one: (i) the twist-class distinctness bookkeeping (4 DISTINCT classes of ONE coset) -- a conflation would inflate the certificate total; (ii) the degeneracy filter IV-4 -- a leak would let a singular quartic count; (iii) the counted-op accounting itself -- an undercount would silently breach the frozen cap.

joints.attack_plan: Re-parse every run manifest under experiments/EXP-ECRANK-76a70d/runs/ against the artifact policy (command, commit, dirty state, env, seeds, inference manifest, stdout/stderr, raw results, validity, timestamps, resources). Re-run the arm B determinism check from the committed seed 760708 and compare the instance list bit-for-bit against the record. Verify the checkpoint cadence (every 10^7 counted ops) appears in the raw outputs, and that any exhaustion report is classified as exhaustion, never as a result.

Agreement is evidence about the quantity; disagreement localises to one of two named implementations and blocks promotion until resolved.

joints.joint: J3 controls, invalidations, and scope honesty

Then attack SCOPE: any language in the executor's records that reads beyond the frozen sample (10^4 seeded b-tuples per arm), beyond the tested n, or toward rank over Q / C1 closure is a finding; rule 6 binds negative outcomes to the exact tested scope.

joints.joint: J4 cost model and exhaustion inertness
joints.attack_plan: Recompute counted-op totals from the raw checkpoint data and compare against the 1.0e8 cap and the 7200 s wall per run; measure actual throughput against finding 2's assumed >= 2 x 10^4 exact Fraction ops/s floor and finding 3's ~7.2 x 10^3 ops/b estimate; verify exhaustion (if any) is inert in BOTH directions -- a slow machine yields a completed prefix plus an exhaustion report, never a fake result and never a silently shortened cap. Check the per-run wall and total budget accounting against the handoff envelope (8 runs max).

blindness.within_round: The validator (369b8d) and the red-team (a2eb0c) may NOT read each other's reports; each attests to what it read. Both read the SNAPSHOT COMMIT of the executor's artifacts (sha named in their task cards) and the frozen contract on main. The Coordinator composes their joint-level verdicts; no whole-claim verdict is taken from either alone.

proves_too_much.failure_signature: The pipeline reports a certified k=3 total >= 8 "from forced classes" for the known-false vector d=(1..1), OR the density metric reports a forcing signal on the scan-stage null objects that does not decay. Either outcome means the argument goes through where its conclusion is known false, and the review round FAILS regardless of arm B's result.
objects: The known-false vector d=(1..1) (IV-1): the certificate pipeline MUST report total = n there. If the pipeline's argument "certified total >= 8 from forced classes" goes through for the known-false object, the argument proves too much and the round fails regardless of arm B's result.
The scan-stage null objects (seed 760711): the density metric must NOT report a forcing signal on null objects; a signal that does not decay on nulls is the canonical artifact tell.

blind_rederivation.what: The certified k=3 total and eigenspace/F_l split for one arm-B instance, re-derived from the spec's statement of the quantity and the instance parameters alone (J2).

procedure_deviations: DEVIATION recorded before the reviewers run (authoritative plan: DEC-20260906-69749a.review_plan, immutable; this queue copy records the departure, and the closing DEC-20260906-7448cf ratifies it). J2 as pre-recorded names "ONE arm-B certified instance (first by seed order)" as its blind re-derivation object. That object DOES NOT EXIST: the executor's terminal receipt records zero constructed instances in every arm (arm B funnel: 80000 draws, 80000 solves_ok, 0 square_ok, 0 found), so there is no certified k=3 total to re-derive. J2 is therefore RE-SCOPED, not dropped, to the only load-bearing quantity the frozen contract still makes blind-re-derivable: control C3 / invalidation rule IV-3 -- (a) the left kernel of W(b) (the n-5 linear relations from the 5 x n Vandermonde) and (b) the delta interpolant, at >= 3 seeded b-tuples PER ARM, re-derived from the STATEMENT of the quantities and the parameters alone. Permitted inputs: the frozen contract's statement of the quantities (experiments/EXP-ECRANK-76a70d/specification.yaml) and the executor's exported blind_rederivation_inputs_C3 blocks in runs/RUN-ECRANK-76a70d-R2-armA/raw-result.json, .../R3-armB/raw-result.json, .../R5-armC/raw-result.json (exported by the contract for exactly this purpose). blind_from is UNCHANGED and still binding: experiments/EXP-ECRANK-76a70d/source/, the run report bodies, and execution-report.yaml must not be opened before the re-derivation is written; the report records sources_read, the blind_from attestation, and the compared quantities (the contract's required C3 artifact), inside the validator's single declared artifact validation-report.md so the ledger archive's declared path set is unchanged. Agreement is evidence about the quantity; disagreement localises to one of two named implementations and triggers IV-3. This discharges BOTH the review-architecture blind re-derivation obligation and the contract's C3 control, which the executor cannot produce because it is inside blind_from.

amendments.reason: tools/validate_ledger.py exits 1 on all eight finalized run manifests of EXP-ECRANK-76a70d ("expected top-level key 'run'"): the executor's drivers wrote FLAT manifests, while check_run requires the nested `run:` record (RUN_REQUIRED_TOP: id, experiment_id, status, code, environment, inputs, timing, result), code.commit, code.command, an honest result.certificate.kind, and the companion files command.txt and environment.json in each run directory. A ledger that does not validate blocks the snapshot archive, so the defect is repaired BEFORE any archive binds, while the manifests are still uncommitted worker output -- no durable record is edited and no supersession entry is created. Root cause is contract wording, not executor error: the frozen required_artifacts clause names "runs/*/manifest.yaml, code.command + code.commit + dirty-tree state" and never names the ledger run schema. The repair is schema conformance only; it is not evidence about H-ECRANK-ee6e0e, not a control failure, and not an invalidation under IV-1..IV-7 (core rules 3 and 5). Chain wiring: archived by the snapshot TASK-20260906-cf7fcf (added to depends_on and archive.source_task_ids, so the snapshot commit binds the repaired bytes), and both blinded reviewers (TASK-20260906-369b8d validator J1/J2, TASK-20260906-a2eb0c red-team J3/J4) now depend on it directly, which is what _validate_review_chains requires for a review_required producer.
